title: Canonical derived inflation and scalar-restriction arrows
statement: For a commutative condensed ring and profinite groups, use the internal action-module categories and normalized invariant equalizers [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], their Grothendieck abelian structures [lem-sfb-condensed-product-bar-comparison], and ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a continuous group homomorphism $\pi:P\to Q$, define exact action restriction by precomposition and its identity normalization on trivial actions. Given normalized invariants $\Gamma_P,\Gamma_Q$, derived objects $X,Y$ and a morphism $\pi^*X\to Y$, define derived inflation to be the derived-adjunction transpose of the restricted counit followed by that morphism. On objects in degree zero use the canonical exact-functor/single-object comparison. Define ordinary invariant inflation by the same ordinary transpose, and the unit from degree-zero invariants to derived invariants by the canonical derived-functor unit. These maps commute with invariant inclusions, degree-zero units and equivariant commutative squares, and are identities for identity restriction. For a morphism of commutative condensed rings use the normalized scalar-action and bar-model interfaces [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Define the derived coefficient arrow by a map to the scalar-restricted object, compatible injective resolutions, the normalized invariant-resolution comparison, and the inverse of the localized scalar-invariant-chain quasi-isomorphism. The scalar and group restriction comparison is uniquely characterized by its identity underlying module maps. The inflation/coefficient square commutes for every normalized scalar restriction and every equivariant inclusion square, independently of the compatible resolutions and lifts.
